head.reference: Jacobs & Hastings, PlantNET Flora of New South Wales, Bromus brevis
head.note: Named species has usually compact 3.5–20 cm panicles, especially at apex, with short rigid ascending branches; do not call all Bromus spikelets loosely dangling.

habit.reference: PlantNET Flora of NSW, exact Bromus brevis; Edgar & Connor (2000), Flora of New Zealand vol. 5
habit.note: Short 30–75 cm tufted plants; sources vary annual/biennial/perennial and PlantNET reports occasional rhizomatous forms. Tuft and observed underground rhizome are conditional positive states, not requirements for every plant.

ligule.reference: Edgar & Connor (2000), Flora of New Zealand, exact Bromus brevis; PlantNET NSW
ligule.note: Leaf-sheath ligule is a torn or denticulate membranous flap, often 1.5–2.5 mm or to 5 mm; neighboring sheath hairs are not a hair-only true ligule.

awns.reference: Jacobs & Hastings, PlantNET NSW Bromus brevis; Flora of New Zealand species description
awns.note: Lemma awns may be completely absent or very short (to 3 mm); a mature spikelet has no conspicuous long awns. Do NOT equate absent obvious long awns with no terminal mucro or minute awn.

taxonomic_source.reference: Kew POWO accepts Bromus brevis Steud.
taxonomic_source.warning: Other authorities including older ITIS treatments apply a broad Bromus catharticus var. rupestris concept. Use Kew's accepted exact species scope for these flora traits; no automatic Hays occurrence.

admission.field_rule: Source-scored literature: Pampas brome is a rather stiff, compact-panicled Bromus with short ascending flowering branches, mostly erect flattened green 9–20 mm spikelets, a ragged membranous ligule and very short or absent awns. Look for a tufted crown (sometimes with rhizomes). Compare B. catharticus and other compressed-spikelet Bromus using glume veins and mature lemma shape. These Australian source-labeled photographs are reference views, NOT a documented Hays plant.
remaining_cautions: No accepted Kew county occurrence or Texas voucher has been established; retain as an introduced source-scored comparison, not Hays native or locally verified.
Alternative older treatments place some material within Bromus catharticus var. rupestris; this profile uses the Kew-accepted B. brevis species and named Australian/New Zealand accounts.
Three source-labeled licensed Australian reference photos preserve original creators and rights; no same-specimen Hays glume measurement or photo-specific identity certification.
Life history and rhizomes are variable in published descriptions; never use missing rhizomes alone to reject the name.

evidence_policy: Exact named-species published characters support literature-scored comparison status only. All four original manifest research source records remain untouched; no native Hays county acceptance, established population or individual gallery photo anatomy is certified.
